messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: P2 - potential sensitive data exposure via API gateway (rule: abnormal egress to third-party endpoint). Incident ID: INC-2026-0421. Root ts 1818256123

sarah.j: I'm on it. Seeing a spike of outbound requests from the gateway to a non-whitelisted domain. Gathering logs now. tagging @sec-eng and @ryan.m

ryan.m: Thanks — I'm pulling recent deploys and gateway config. Any customer-facing evidence yet?

maria.cs: Not yet. CS: we should prep a holding statement in case customers ask. Low-level impact for now until we confirm payloads.

sec-eng: I have a quick triage: initial flow shows malformed header that caused a routing rule to forward artifacts. Looks like a misconfigured integration service account. Capturing pcap + request IDs.

sec-eng: Quick mitigation: blocking outbound to that domain at the edge now (w/ACL). Applying WAF rule 3332 to drop suspicious header patterns.

incident-bot: Action recorded: ACL applied to domain bad.example.net (edge). WAF rule 3332 applied.

ryan.m: Good. Sarah can you take a look at S3 / KV logs for any keys referenced? Need to scope whether tokens/PII were in those requests.

sarah.j: Query running: `select * from api_audit where dest='bad.example.net' and ts > 1818256000` — will paste results shortly.

sarah.j: Quick paste of results (sanitized):
```
count: 8
paths: [ /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings ]
headers: some include x-correlation-id, user-agent; no Authorization header observed in plain text
payload-snippets: truncated, some user-provided prompt text present
```

sec-eng: Not great — prompt text could contain customer content. We need to assume potential exposure of user-provided strings until we confirm. Escalating to Legal for notification guidance.

legal: On it. Need exact scope (customers, time window, data types). Please capture sample request IDs and whether API keys or auth tokens were sent. If tokens were leaked, treat as higher severity.

maria.cs: I'll start drafting a holding customer message. Suggest: say we detected an incident, we blocked it, investigating, no confirmed account takeover, will notify affected customers within 72 hours once scope known.

ops-lead: Please don't send anything externally until Legal signs off. Internal comms only for now.

ben.s: On-call rotation bot: @oncall-rotation-bot handoff scheduled in 30m. If this persists, prepare to escalate to P1.

sarah.j: Update: of the 8 requests, 3 contained free-text prompts that look like customer content. No API keys in payload bodies. Auth was via short-lived bearer token in TLS; we have no evidence tokens were exfiltrated in cleartext.

sec-eng: We should assume user prompt text may have been included. Containment done (block + revoke service account key used by that misconfigured integration). Rotating that key now.

incident-bot: Audit note: service account `integration-data-forwarder` key rotated by sarah.j at 1818256520.

ryan.m: For the status page, propose we post a "Investigating" update with limited details: don't call it data exposure until scope confirmed. Draft: 
"We are investigating an issue affecting outbound requests from our API gateway. We have implemented mitigations and are actively analyzing request logs to determine whether customer data was sent to an external endpoint. We will provide updates as our investigation progresses."

maria.cs: Draft customer notification template (for review by Legal):
---
Hi <CustomerName>,

We are contacting you to let you know we are investigating a potential security incident that may have resulted in customer-provided content being sent to an external endpoint. We have implemented containment steps and are actively assessing the scope. At this time we have not confirmed unauthorized access to your account. We will follow up within 72 hours with an update and any recommended next steps.

If you have urgent concerns, contact support@redwood.com and we will prioritize your case.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Trust & Safety
---

legal: Change: please avoid the phrase "potential security incident" in external comms; prefer "service incident potentially affecting customer-provided content". Also add a line about what we're doing: blocking the endpoint, rotating integration keys, and reviewing logs. Keep it short.

maria.cs: Updated draft incorporating legal notes:
---
Hi <CustomerName>,

We are currently investigating a service incident that may have resulted in customer-provided content being sent to an external endpoint. We have blocked the endpoint, rotated the affected integration key, and are reviewing request logs to determine the scope of impact. At this time we have not confirmed unauthorized access to your account. We will provide an update within 72 hours.

If you have urgent concerns, contact support@redwood.com.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Trust & Safety
---

ops-lead: Good. Legal: do we need to notify regulators or will that wait until scope is confirmed?

legal: Regulator notification depends on data types and jurisdictions. If we confirm personal data exfiltration for EU/UK/CA residents, we'll follow breach reporting timelines. For now, prepare an internal timeline + list of potentially affected customers so we can assess legal obligations quickly.

sec-eng: Running targeted grep across archived logs for the time window 1818256000-1818256600. Will share IDs and sample payloads in a controlled channel #sec-evidence only.

sarah.j: Prep task list for handoff to next on-call in 30m:
- containment actions performed (ACL applied, WAF rule, key rotated)
- list of request IDs and sanitized snippets uploaded to #sec-evidence
- status page draft (needs signoff): INVESTIGATING message above
- customer notification template (legal-approved) ready to send once legal signs
- CS hold queue created and flagged for priority outreach if affected
- timeline and runbook pinned in thread

oncall-rotation-bot: @ryan.m you are tagged as next on-call starting 1818257923. Handoff window 30m.

ryan.m: I'll take the handoff. Sarah, leave exact grep queries and ACL rollback steps in the thread. Also note: if further evidence shows tokens in plaintext, escalate to P1 and contact customers immediately.

sarah.j: Pasted grep query and ACL rollback snippet:
```
# grep for dest and timeframe
jq '. | select(.dest=="bad.example.net" and .ts>=1818256000 and .ts<=1818256600)' /var/log/api_audit.jsonl

# ACL remove
redwood-edge acl remove bad.example.net --id 3332
```

sec-eng: Evidence summary to handoff: 8 requests, 3 with user text. No plaintext tokens found. Blocked endpoint and rotated key. Next steps: full review of archived payloads, notify Legal + CS for the small set of customers whose prompts appear in requests.

legal: When you have the list of customer IDs, send to legal via secure doc (not slack). We'll review and advise on regulator notification and customer notice language adjustments.

maria.cs: CS: I'll prepare outreach templates for affected customers and triage guide for support to mark urgency.

ben.s: Confirming handoff notes saved to incident tracker INC-2026-0421. Next on-call (ryan.m) acknowledged. If new exfil detected escalate.

ryan.m: Acknowledged. I'll post the status page update once Legal signs off on language. For now internal status: MITIGATED (edge block + key rotation) / INVESTIGATING (scope).

sarah.j: Final note before handoff: keep #incidents notif muted for large noise; route evidence to #sec-evidence. I'll be reachable if anything pops during handoff.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 updated: state=mitigated; assignee=ryan.m; last_update=1818257080

maria.cs: Thanks everyone — please react with :thumbsup: when you've reviewed the customer template so Legal knows to move to distribution once secure list provided.

legal: Reviewed. :thumbsup:

ryan.m: Taking over. I'll coordinate next steps and schedule an update window at +3h.

sarah.j: handing off now — thread locked for operational notes only.
